data.title: Prudential Financial's PGIM launches two core equity ETFs
data.description:
Prudential Financial's (PRU) $1.5 trillion asset management arm, PGIM, has launched two new core equity exchange-traded funds.

The ETFs are the PGIM Jennison Small-Mid Cap Core Equity ETF (PJSM) and the PGIM Jennison International Core Equity ETF (PJIN).

PJSM is expected to invest at least 80% of its investable assets in equity and equity-related securities of small- and medium-capitalization companies.

PJIN is focused on issuers that are non-U.S. companies.

"Core equity investing is often viewed as a choice between active conviction and benchmark discipline, but the reality is that investors don't have to sacrifice one for the other," said Ken Moore, head of Jennison, an investment group within PGIM.

"We draw on decades of bottom-up, fundamental research experience and a global opportunity set to identify opportunities that may be overlooked by purely index-based approaches," added Moore.

data.title: Data center pushback: A key issue for midterms
data.description:
The data center boom is becoming a major issue in the upcoming midterm elections, with local communities pushing back on construction plans amid concerns over electricity rates and environmental impact.

Around 75 data center projects worth about $130B were blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 due to local opposition, according to the Data Center Watch.

And state lawmakers are responding – at least 375 bills on data centers have been introduced this year, The Washington Post's analysis of legislative records found. Around three-quarters of these bills seek to restrict data centers in some way.

According to the National Conference of State Legislatures, 15 U.S. states have considered moratoriums or bans on data centers this year. So far, only New York has passed a one-year moratorium on the construction of large new data centers.

A recent Gallup survey found that seven in 10 Americans oppose constructing data centers for AI in their local area. And candidates running for office in the midterms are latching on to the issue, especially since affordability is now the top issue for voters.

"Candidates in both parties are increasingly running ads against data centers, framing opponents as indifferent to community concerns over their construction," Nicol Lee and Darrell West, both senior fellows in the Governance Studies program at the Brookings Institution, wrote.

"The economy is a central issue in this election, and candidates are therefore packaging affordability, data centers, and electric rate increases into a single narrative and using it to criticize tech development," they added.

Mounting local opposition is driven by concerns over data centers' electricity consumption, water use, land availability and environmental impacts.

Utilities are receiving hundreds of gigawatts in interconnection requests for data centers, which will further strain the power grid. To meet the surge in demand, utilities need to invest more in infrastructure such as power lines and transformers.

And to cover these investments, many utilities are passing on the costs to their customers. 

Meanwhile, large data centers can consume up to 5M gallons per day for cooling servers, according to the Environmental and Energy Study Institute (EESI). That’s equivalent to the water use of a town populated by 10,000-50,000 people.

"Infrastructure bottlenecks, supply chain constraints, uncertainty around AI monetization, growing physical climate risks, regulatory hurdles and community opposition will increasingly determine where and how AI infrastructure is built," Allianz Commercial said.

Notable hyperscalers: Amazon (AMZN), Microsoft (MSFT), Google (GOOG) (GOOGL), Meta (META), Oracle (ORCL), CoreWeave (CRWV).

data.title: DNO drops takeover bid for Genel Energy after scooping up Capricorn
data.description:
Genel Energy (GEGYF) plunged 14.6% in London trading Friday after Norwegian oil and gas operator DNO (DTNOF) (DTNOY) said it will not make an offer to acquire its British peer.

In August, DNO (FTNOF) (FTNOY) made a 69 pence/share takeover approach that valued Genel (GEGYF) at £202M, which the U.K. company dismissed on the grounds that it "fundamentally undervalues" the business; since then, DNO said Genel has "demonstrated no willingness to engage."

Under U.K. takeover rules, DNO (DTNOF) (DTNOY) had until September 4 to announce a firm intention to make an offer for Genel (GEGYF) or walk away.

Earlier this week, DTO (DTNOF) (DTNOY) trumped a bid by Genel (GEGYF) for Capricorn Energy, agreeing on a deal that valued the British oil and gas E&P company at $396M; Genel had previously reached an agreement to acquire Capricorn for ~$360M.

data.title: August payroll breadth hits highest level since late 2024
data.description:
In a reassuring sign for the U.S. labor market, employment breadth was solidly positive in August, reaching its strongest level since December 2024, according to Charles Schwab's Kevin Gordon.

Specifically, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' Employment Diffusion Index for nonfarm payrolls climbed to 55.6, indicating that job creation remains widespread across the economy. A reading above 50 indicates expansion, while a print below 50 signals contraction.

While the headline diffusion index underscores broad-based hiring, underlying sector data provides important context for this growth. Between July and August 2026, the leisure and hospitality industry drove the strongest gains by adding 62K jobs, followed by government with 35K and private education and health services with 29K.

However, the expansion was not entirely universal. The information sector notably shed 23K jobs, and financial activities saw a decrease of 11K positions.

Overall, nonfarm payrolls increased by 162K, far exceeding the +55K consensus and +21K in the prior month, which was revised from -23K.

data.title: Dianthus gains new Buy from Citi on multi-blockbuster potential for lead drug
data.description:
Citi on Friday issued a new Buy rating on Dianthus Therapeutics (DNTH), a biotech developing drugs for autoimmune conditions, citing a multibillion-dollar peak sales opportunity for its lead candidate, claseprubart.

The New York-based Dianthus is developing the complement inhibitor as a pipeline-in-a-product targeting a range of autoimmune disorders, including generalized myasthenia gravis, chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy, and multifocal motor neuropathy.

Analyst Samantha Semenkow projected more than $5B in peak adjusted global sales for Claseprubart, noting that the drug has already established a competitive efficacy profile thanks to proof-of-concept data in gMG and CIDP.

The analyst issued a $156 per share target on the stock, projecting ~$2.5B and $2.4B in peak U.S. unadjusted revenue for claseprubart in gMG and CIDP, respectively.

“Given claseprubart’s efficacious, safe, and convenient dosing profile, we see potential for broad uptake both as a best-in-class complement inhibitor and more broadly as a first-line or preferred second-line biologic,” Semenkow wrote.

She added that with its two next-gen, dual-mechanism candidates, DNTH212 and DNTH312, the company is broadening its autoimmune franchise into rheumatology and other areas, which give it “longer-term optionality for continued growth.”

data.title: Gold’s fiscal-policy message stays clear as deficits worsen
data.description:
Gold had historically performed better when the U.S. budget balance was deteriorating, according to Rob Anderson, U.S. sector strategist at NDR Research.

“Since 1980, gold has returned 7.2% annualized when the U.S. budget balance was deteriorating, versus a 2.0% gain when it was improving,” Anderson said in a post on X.

The accompanying chart, based on Bloomberg Finance data, showed gold prices alongside the U.S. federal government budget balance from 1979 through July 2026.

The chart classified periods by the direction of the six-month change in the annualized budget balance. Gold had gained an annualized 7.21% during periods when the budget balance was worsening, compared with 1.99% when it was improving.

Periods with a worsening budget balance accounted for 47.73% of the observations shown, while improving periods accounted for 52.27%.

The chart also showed the federal government budget balance had remained in deficit for much of the period, with the latest reading at -$1,945.7B as of July 31, 2026.

Gold had also climbed sharply in the most recent portion of the chart, reaching a level above the $5,000 mark before pulling back.

Anderson said the historical relationship suggested that the "debasement trade" could remain a long-term tailwind for gold.

data.title: Asana, Guidewire and UiPath lead enterprise software stocks down following earnings
data.description:
Asana (ASAN), Guidewire (GWRE), and UiPath (PATH) plunged following their latest earnings results during early market action on Friday as much of the enterprise software sector slipped into the red.

All three stocks had dropped more than 10%.

Asana reported a slightly better-than-expected second quarter, with net new annual recurring revenue from AI products increasing 25%. However, analysts noted headwinds from its Product-Led Growth, or PLG, strategy.

"ASAN delivered modest upside to F2Q results, yet only partly flowed the upside to the guide as PLG headwinds persisted, along with a timing impact from AI product pricing/packaging changes," said Citi analysts in a Friday investor note. "NN ARR from AI products expanded to 25% from 17% in F1Q with new agentic products rolling out through the year, including a new Agentic Work Management (AWM) package that bundles Teammates, Studio, and Dash into every paid tier and triggering the shift in rev rec timing ($1.2M for F2H). While we had expected ASAN to have made more progress in counteracting PLG challenges, we note accelerating enterprise fundamentals and a material contribution from AI already."

Citi retained its Buy rating and edged up its price target on Asana to $12 from $11.

Meanwhile, Guidewire tanked more than 15% following its fourth-quarter results, as analysts were divided on its ARR growth.

"FY27 ARR outlook calls for $1,450-$1,460M / ~18% y/y cc growth vs. 19% y/y cc exiting FY26 & roughly bracketing prior consensus of $1,454M," said Wells Fargo analyst Michael Turrin in a note. "This implies ~$213M in NNARR (midpoint), roughly in-line w/ ~$210M in FY26, w/ growth in-line w/ its stated 17-18% FY25-FY28 target CAGR. Revs guidance includes total revs of $1,707-1,727M (~1% above consensus at the midpt) on ~16-17% growth with subs +31% y/y, maintenance down ~15%, license down ~20% & prof svcs up ~6%."

Wells Fargo maintained its Overweight rating and inched up its price target to $195 from $190.

However, Citi said the “modest” ARR outlook “overshadowed” a solid fourth quarter for the provider of software for the property and casualty insurance industry.

"Turning to FY27 guidance, ARR growth of 18% y/y cc growth at the midpoint was in-line with consensus but based on our conversation with buy-side investors missed their expectations given the 5 pt disconnect from FY26 fully ramped ARR," Citi analysts noted.

Citi retained its Neutral rating on the stock and increased its target price to $181 from $137.

UiPath also sank more than 10% despite its second-quarter earnings topping estimates as the beat wasn't as strong as it has been.

"FQ2 rev topped the high end of guide by $10M/~3%, a touch below the magnitude of recent beats," said Wells Fargo analyst Michael Turrin in an investor note. "Rev growth of 13% y/y benefited from $8M of FX tailwind in the quarter, or 11% ex-FX. NNARR of $37M beat by $4M, roughly consistent w/ prior patterns (last 5 quarters trending in the $2-6M beat range). While NNARR added was $36M when backing out $1M y/y FX tailwind (vs. $30M in 2Q'26), the comp was its 2nd lowest NNARR quarter ever as a public co."

Wells Fargo retained its Equal Weight rating and nudged up its price target to $15 from $13.

Similarly, Oppenheimer maintained its Neutral rating, highlighting that evidence of reacceleration is limited. 

"On balance, the quarter beat is low quality (i.e., from services outperforming and expense discipline rather than an acceleration in demand), the growth for the business is decelerating toward low double digits, and NRR growth remains in single digits," said Oppenheimer analyst Brian Schwartz in a note. "In our view, these items are unlikely to mitigate concerns that intensifying competition in the agentic era from the mega IT and frontier model suppliers will weaken the company's moat and limit long-term growth."

UiPath also promoted Hitesh Ramani as its new chief financial officer. He replaces Ashim Gupta, who will now serve exclusively as chief operating officer. Gupta had held both executive roles for the past two years.

However, it wasn't a bad day for Samsara, whose share climbed 6% after increasing its guidance.

Docusign (DOCU) slid 1% following its second-quarter earnings results. Shares initially popped up 7% during post-market trading on Thursday after the company demonstrated AI momentum and raised its forecast.

"Management raised FY27 guidance as visibility and underlying trends improved in 2Q following a more measured outlook after 1Q," said Citi analysts in a Friday note. "Supporting data points included faster account growth, DNR rounding up and growth in IAM as a percentage of ARR."

Citi has a Neutral rating and $72 price target on Docusign.

Needham also retained its Hold rating on the stock.

Overall, the software sector was down, as evidenced by the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (IGV), declining nearly 2%.

data.title: Wall Street slides after investors received the latest payrolls print
data.description:
Wall Street's major market averages shifted lower after traders and investors digested the the latest jobs data which came in stronger than forecasted.

The blue-chip Dow (DJI) was last -0.4%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last -0.1%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) was last +0.1%. 

From a sector-by-sector standpoint, just three of the 11 S&P segments were in the green and were led by information technology. At the other end, energy was the weakest performer. 

On the economic front, the August U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased by +162K versus the +55K consensus figure, according to data released by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. At the same time, the unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%, compared to the 4.2% forecasted level. 

Treasury yields are on the move higher. The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield (US2Y) moved up 4 basis points to 4.38%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield (US10Y) was higher by 1 basis point to 4.77%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield (US30Y) inched up 1 basis point to 5.24%. 

As for stocks that were on the move, shares of KLA Corporation (KLAC) climbed higher by +7.5%, while shares of Lululemon (LULU) fell -18.1%.

data.title: Industrial stocks face broader weakness as bear-market breadth hits 2025 High
data.description:
Turning Point Market Research says the percentage of S&P 500 industrial stocks trading in a bear market has climbed to 45%, surpassing the 43% reached at the March low and marking the highest level since the 2025 Liberation Day selloff.

The deterioration is notable because the broader S&P 500 Industrials index remains near elevated levels, suggesting that headline sector performance may be masking increasing weakness among individual constituents.

The chart from Turning Point Market Research shows the percentage of industrial stocks trading more than 20% below their 252-day highs rising to 45.57%. The indicator has also formed a series of higher lows and higher highs in recent months, pointing to a gradual broadening of weakness. The latest reading has moved above the level seen around the March market low, underscoring the deterioration in sector breadth.

Against this backdrop, the S&P 500 Industrial index (XLI) offers a snapshot of the companies carrying the largest weights in the industrial sector. The ETF has 87 holdings, with its 10 largest positions collectively accounting for 39.59% of the portfolio. Caterpillar is the largest holding at 6.67%, followed by General Electric at 6.36% and RTX at 5.08%.

The top 10 holdings of XLI are:

  • Caterpillar (CAT) — 6.67%
  • General Electric (GE) — 6.36%
  • RTX (RTX) — 5.08%
  • GE Vernova (GEV) — 4.39%
  • Union Pacific (UNP) — 3.24%
  • Deere & Co. (DE) — 2.99%
  • Boeing (BA) — 2.98%
  • Eaton (ETN) — 2.84%
  • Uber Technologies (UBER) — 2.80%
